clue.text: Liverpool, that place down south

blocks.note: a place over yonder is there
D is the standard abbreviation for down
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Someone describes the city of Liverpool as a place somewhere down in the south of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool is the football club here, not the city, so the geography is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reds is the long-standing nickname of Liverpool Football Club, after their red home shirts.

clue.text: President Trump's got his head up rear end, ...

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the name is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the surname
aft is the rear end of a ship

explanation.surface: A jibe that President Trump has his head stuck somewhere unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' puts T at the top, above AFT. The ellipsis runs the sentence on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: William Howard Taft was the twenty-seventh President of the United States, serving from 1909 to 1913.

clue.text: ... eighth rank and as crooked as they are critical

indicators.note: something crooked is bent out of its true line, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: presidents of low rank are as crooked as their critics claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Something earth-shaking is momentous and of huge consequence, which is what a critical matter is.

clue.text: Analysts care about being introduced to students not having a first

indicators.note: turned about suggests the word is spun round into a fresh arrangement
losing the first means the opening letter of the word is dropped
something introduced into a group goes inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: the four letters of care rearranged
freshers are first-year university students in Britain

explanation.surface: Analysts take care over how they are introduced to students who lack a first-class degree.
explanation.walkthrough: Freshers loses its F to leave RESHERS, and the jumbled care goes in after RES. 'A first' looks like a degree class but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Researchers are people who study and examine data or sources in detail, which is the work of analysts.

clue.text: Not even real! Totally sounding dodgy

indicators.note: the letters that are not in even positions are the odd ones, so every other letter is kept starting with the first

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a claim is totally dodgy and not even real.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattly car or machine makes loose clattering noises, which is how something sounds when it seems unsound or suspect.

clue.text: Starters for England and Manchester United, they were on hand for Hull

definitions.text: they were on hand for Hull
definitions.note: plural phrase for a singular answer: 'they' stands loosely for the puppet

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: opening letter
opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: Football talk: England and Manchester United players turning out for Hull City.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is not the football club but Rod Hull, a British TV entertainer whose act was a bird glove puppet worn on his arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod Hull performed with a puppet named Emu on his arm, so the bird was literally on hand for him.

clue.text: See 1
That lady's love and the love of a legendarily tragic swimmer

definitions.text: the love of a legendarily tragic swimmer

blocks.note: the possessive belonging to a woman
love is zero in tennis, a round O

explanation.surface: A tale of a woman's love and a doomed swimmer from legend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit his beloved and drowned in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Hero was the priestess loved by Leander, the mythical swimmer who drowned crossing the strait to reach her.

clue.text: See 10
Initially shoots rifle, recoiling a bit

indicators.note: only a bit of the following words is used, a run of letters sitting inside them
a rifle recoils by kicking backwards, so the run of letters is read right to left

blocks.note: the closing pair of letters of shoots and the opening trio of rifle

explanation.surface: A rifle kicks back a little when it first fires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something first means doing it at the start, before anything else, just as initially does.

clue.text: It's hell, or what might get you there

blocks.note: first meaning: an ordeal
second meaning: a mortal sin that could send you to the infernal regions

explanation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to hell, so the second meaning is the crime that would damn you.
explanation.definitionFit: Murder is an informal word for a gruelling experience, and also the killing that would condemn a sinner to damnation.

clue.text: Citizen Kane writer's marriage announced from northern city

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so we want words as they are heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: Herman Mankiewicz, known as Mank, co-wrote the film's script; marriage is a union

explanation.surface: News of the wedding of the man who wrote Citizen Kane, reported from a northern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Citizen' tempts as the definition, but it belongs to the film title.
explanation.definitionFit: Mancunian is the adjective for people and things from Manchester, a major city in northern England.

clue.text: A hybrid model or SEAT with electric lead

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the letters are fashioned into a new form
the lead of a word is its front, so just its opening letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A car advert: a hybrid model, or a SEAT, the Spanish car brand, with an electric drive.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAT is a car maker, so 'hybrid' and 'electric' point to cars, not plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea roses are hybrid garden roses, and hybrid teas are the most popular class of cultivated rose.

clue.text: They produce oil to go over muscle

blocks.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: Producers of oil set out to dominate, flexing their muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: OPEC is the cartel of petroleum-exporting countries, the nations that pump much of the world's crude.

clue.text: Moral panic to run amok for crying out loud

indicators.note: running amok is wild disorder, so the letters career about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A moral panic spreads wildly, for crying out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For crying out loud' reads as an exasperated exclamation; 'for' is the link and the rest is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A proclamation is a public announcement declared loudly, literally a crying out of news to everyone.

clue.text: Win a BBC tape edited to show Channel swimmer

indicators.note: an edited tape has its material cut and rearranged, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get a BBC recording cut to feature a cross-Channel swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Webb, a merchant navy captain, was the first recorded person to swim the English Channel unaided, in 1875.

clue.text: Online business with €2m in force

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the doubled letter goes within the word for compel

blocks.note: the euro sign reads as the letter E
to coerce is to force
two of the letter M

explanation.surface: An internet company backed by two million euros is a force to be reckoned with.
explanation.walkthrough: '2m' looks like two million but just means the letter M twice; 'in force' is not the legal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: E-commerce is trade conducted over the internet, buying and selling goods through websites.

clue.text: Mr Aykroyd's hugging with lady to start

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap the arms around, so one piece is held inside the name

blocks.note: Dan Aykroyd, the Ghostbusters actor
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: The actor Dan Aykroyd embraces a woman as things get going.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also a woman's name, so 'lady' adds a nod to the result alongside the definition 'start'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the first appearance of daylight, and figuratively the beginning or birth of anything.

clue.text: By installing CIA predecessor becomes authoritarian

indicators.note: installing something puts it inside a building or system, so one piece is fitted within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the Office of Strategic Services, the US wartime spy agency replaced by the CIA

explanation.surface: A regime turns dictatorial by setting up a forerunner of the CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bossy person is domineering and keen to give orders, the same overbearing manner as an authoritarian.

clue.text: Madge and Harold see clergy, ...

blocks.note: first meaning: the married couple Madge and Harold in the Australian soap Neighbours, whose surname this is
second meaning: senior churchmen who each oversee a diocese

explanation.surface: Two people go to visit the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' joins the two meanings while hinting at a diocese, also called a see; the ellipsis carries on into the next clue's chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishops are senior clergy in charge of dioceses, and the Neighbours couple share that family surname.

clue.text: Bird, initially at height, dropping back, floating on air

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the first letter of the short word is kept
going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: a male fowl
the first letter
H is the abbreviation for height
a bird dropping is poo

explanation.surface: A bird high up, dropping back down, glides on the air currents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' looks like a falling motion but is the noun, as in bird droppings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cock-a-hoop means being jubilant and elated, the same delight as feeling you are floating on air.

clue.text: Loose cannons lack enforcement to some extent

indicators.note: only to some extent means only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the run from the end of the first word into the start of the third

explanation.surface: Loose cannons partly lack anyone to rein them in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' is a verb here, to let go or ease off, not the adjective of 'loose cannons'.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken a rope or grip is to loosen it, easing off the tension, which is what the verb loose means.

clue.text: ... they're on board with this man not wanting a mate

definitions.text: this man not wanting a mate

blocks.clueFragment: this man not wanting a mate
blocks.note: surface reading: a lonely bachelor who wants no partner
setter's reading: a chess piece whose aim is to avoid checkmate, sharing the board with the clergy of the previous clue

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back: 'they' are the bishops of the previous clue, which share the chessboard with this piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the most important piece is the one that must escape checkmate, so it is literally a man not wanting a mate.

clue.text: Brown paper's boring! You can multiply that by 200 for starters

indicators.note: multiplying the opening value changes it into another numeral, so the starter of the word is swapped for a new one

blocks.note: vanilla means plain and unexciting
V is Roman five, and five times two hundred is a thousand, Roman M

explanation.surface: Someone complains that brown wrapping paper is dull, then offers a sum about multiplying it.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening V of the word for boring is read as the Roman numeral five; times 200 it becomes M, for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Manilla is the strong buff-coloured paper used for envelopes and folders, originally made from Manila hemp.

clue.text: Adjust nothing, not a thing, in French gallery

blocks.note: a zero looks like O
the French word for nothing
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Change nothing, not one thing, in a gallery in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In French' attaches only to 'not a thing', not to the gallery, which is London's.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate something is to align or position it correctly, which is to adjust it to its proper bearings.

clue.text: Tough guy, one on the edge

indicators.note: in an across entry one thing on another comes after it, so the word for one is placed second

blocks.note: a hem is the folded edge of cloth
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A hard man who lives on the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'one on the edge' puts the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A he-man is a strongly built, very masculine fellow, the stereotypical tough guy.

clue.text: Poet from Derby perhaps removing central triplet

indicators.note: removing the central triplet takes out the three letters in the very middle of the word

blocks.note: the Derby is a famous English flat race at Epsom

explanation.surface: A poet hailing from the city of Derby, minus three members of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the Midlands city but is the Epsom horse race; dropping its middle three letters SER leaves the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was the leading Roman lyric poet of the reign of Augustus, author of the Odes.

clue.text: Long yarn to droop down and across

blocks.note: to sag is to droop downwards
A is the crossword abbreviation for across

explanation.surface: A story long enough to make the listener sag in all directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down and across' sounds like crossword directions, but only across gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long, rambling story or an epic family chronicle, so a long yarn in the storytelling sense.

clue.text: The Feds need to change their leader for one, agreed?

indicators.text: need to change their leader for
indicators.note: changing the leader swaps the opening letter of the word for another one

blocks.note: G-men are FBI agents, US federal officers
a, the article, means one

explanation.surface: FBI agents must replace their boss with someone else; does everyone concur?
explanation.definitionFit: Saying amen expresses assent, as the congregation's word of agreement at the end of a prayer.

clue.text: Account concerning land

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for account
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A report about some land.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of area and, in older usage, a field or plot, so acres stand for land holdings.

clue.text: Hey! By the way ... by the way ...

blocks.note: a postscript adds a by-the-way afterthought to a letter
read as next to a road: the way is St, short for street

explanation.surface: Someone trying to get attention with a pair of casual asides.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is read two ways: first as the postscript abbreviation, then as 'the way' meaning a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the hissing sound used to catch someone's attention quietly, just like a hushed hey.

clue.text: Miranda drops off chaps in motor

indicators.note: dropping something off means leaving it behind, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: Carmen Miranda, the singer famed for her fruit hats
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A woman named Miranda gives some men a lift in her car.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname leads to Carmen Miranda, the Brazilian samba singer and film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor is an informal British word for a car, as in a nice new motor.

clue.text: See 13
Keep or throw away French article

blocks.note: to cast off is to throw away
le is the French masculine for the

explanation.surface: A choice between keeping something and throwing it away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb opposite 'throw away', but it is the noun for a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the main tower or stronghold of a fortress, and by extension a castle itself.

clue.text: Tip a quantity of liquid for short one in jug

indicators.note: tipping something up turns it over, so in a down clue the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.clueFragment: a quantity of liquid for short
blocks.note: the abbreviation for gallon

explanation.surface: Instructions to pour a measure of liquid, briefly, into a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: Jug is slang for prison, so the one in jug is a convict; an old lag is a habitual prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A lag is British slang for a convict or prisoner, especially in the phrase old lag.

clue.text: Come up with the third person to be inside the second

indicators.note: inside places one verb form within the other, enclosed by its letters

blocks.note: the second-person form of to be, as in you are
the third-person form of to be, as in she is

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a third person ending up inside a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces come from conjugating the verb to be: 'the second' means its second-person form.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to get up or emerge, so it means to come up, whether from bed or as an issue.

clue.text: Dick will do it to get going around half five

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is two of its letters, here the back pair
going around something encloses it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to instigate is to set something in motion
the latter half of the word

explanation.surface: A man is ready to get moving at half past five.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick is old slang for a detective, as in private dick. Half five looks like a time, but takes two letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Investigating crimes is exactly what a detective, or private dick, does for a living.

clue.text: A tip for writing note about setter

indicators.note: about means round the outside, so the first piece encloses the second

blocks.note: nota bene, Latin for note well
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: Advice on writing: the setter leaves a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A tip for writing' reads like advice but means the pointed end of a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A nib is the metal point of a fountain pen that touches the paper, literally the writing tip.
